ADJOURNED EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
  MINUTES
  February 26, 2018

CALL TO ORDER
CHAIRMAN MITCHELL called the meeting to order, the time being 6:01 p.m. in the Rolling
Hills Estates City Council Chambers.

COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT
Chairman Judy Mitchell
Susan Brtis
Patricia Harik
Bill Kemp
Lou Persichina
Vicki Shinn
Carrie Silvano

STAFF MEMBER PRESENT
Andy Clark, Community Services Director

DRAFT MINUTES OF DECEMBER 18, 2017
MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER SILVANO

  TO APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF THE DECEMBER 18, 2017 EQUESTRIAN
  COMMITTEE MEETING AS PRESENTED.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL SO ORDERED.

AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA
Eden Fizulich, 26302 Birchfield Avenue, RPV notified the Equestrian Committee that a free
Equine Emergency Preparedness Demonstration focused on large animal evacuation
planning would be held in Arena #1 in Ernie Howlett Park on March 24, 2018 from 2:00 to
4:00 p.m. The Committee discussed a variety of methods to promote this event.

CALIFORNIA WATER SERVICE COMPANY WATER RELIABILITY PROJECT MONTHLY
UPDATE
Equestrian Committee Representative, MEMBER SHINN, reported that she would be
attending their next meeting on February 28, 2018 and therefore had no report.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
FEBRUARY 26, 2018  1
 Nancy Wildman, 34 Pony Lane, RHE who is providing consulting services for California Water
Service Company regarding the temporary relocation of horses from her neighborhood,
reported that Gil Houle was finalizing contracts with a barn construction company to install
temporary boarding facilities to relocate horses along trails having the new water pipes
installed at the cost of California Water Service Company.

2018 MAYOR’S BREAKFAST RIDE PARTICIPATION MEASURES
The Community Services Director thanked audience member, Nancy Wildman, for information
resulting in finding a horse rental vendor to provide horses for elected officials this year. He
then highlighted the Equestrian Committee’s measures to improve local equestrian
participation developed in May 2017. MEMBER SILVANO told audience members that City
Council was very disappointed with last year’s small turn-out of equestrians and warned them
that their support of the City’s long equestrian heritage could decrease if this trend continued.

Regarding utilizing better publicity measures, several suggestions were made including: 1)
develop a good flyer that will attract area riders and post in all locations that equestrians
gather; 2) consider promoting the event in Peninsula People magazine; 3) in addition to
putting an article in the PVPHA Dispatch, Nancy Wildman stated that she will send out several
email reminders to their membership; 4) invite the Los Caballeros organization members to
join the ride this year; 5) licensed Horse Trainers will be mailed an event flyer to invite them
and their students to participate; 6) promote the event on NextDoor and PV Patch; 7) use the
City’s website ListServe to notify those who request information regarding Equestrian
Committee meetings; and 8) promote the event to the City’s various dog training class
instructors since the event will be expanded to include hikers, joggers, and dog walkers.

The Committee discussed how dog walkers, joggers, and hikers could be involved for the first
time and agreed that this group of trail users should start about 30 minutes ahead of the riders
so that horses are not spooked by a group of individuals and dogs coming up from behind the
riders. MEMBER SHINN suggested that resident, Kelly Yates, be the Ride Leader this year.
Audience member, Sean Martin, indicated that he would lead the ride if Kelly couldn’t. He
also suggested and volunteered to coordinate an “Equestrian Play Day” following the Scout
Pancake Breakfast in an Ernie Howlett Park arena to encourage more riders to participate.
The Committee liked this idea and recommended that the “Play Day” be simple fun events
and promoted in all the Mayor’s Breakfast Ride promotions.

In response to CHAIRMAN MITCHELL’S inquiry, the Committee felt that City Council
Members and any guest elected officials should conduct the new “meet and greet” session
next to the Chandler Park arena where the Mayor’s Breakfast Ride starts.

LICENSED HORSE TRAINER BACKGROUND CHECKS
The Community Services Director reported that the City Attorney had indicated that there was
low risk for the City in regards to Horse Trainers, who indemnify the City with a Certificate of
General Liability insurance, for the City to incur claims. However, the City Attorney stated that
an Ordinance could be adopted by City Council requiring Horse Trainers to have criminal
background checks completed and reviewed by the Lomita Sheriff Station.
EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
FEBRUARY 26, 2018  2
 MEMBER HARIK stated that CPA’s must now have a criminal background check, but felt that
there was little chance that a child could be molested while riding a horse in a public arena.
MEMBER SILVANO concurred, but noted that child molestations usually occurred before or
after sport practices or competitions rather than while the activity was taking place. She also
felt if the Committee moved forward with recommending criminal background checks for
Horse Trainers, that the City should require them for every business that involves contact with
children.

CHAIRMAN MITCHELL observed that there did not seem much Committee support for
making a recommendation to City Council to require criminal background checks in order to
obtain a Horse Trainers Business License and Permit to use the public arenas. The
Community Services Director noted that Horse Trainers would also have to incur an additional
fee for the background check services.

MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER HARIK

  TO NOT REQUIRE LICENSED HORSE TRAINERS TO COMPLETE A CRIMINAL
  BACKGROUND CHECK IN ORDER TO USE THE CITY’S PUBLIC HORSE ARENAS
  AT THIS TIME.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL SO ORDERED.

SEAHORSE RIDING CLUB SALE
MEMBER SHINN reported that the sale of this private boarding and training facility was in
escrow. Further, that it was the intent of the buyer to attempt to have the property re-zoned
for the development of an office building. She noted that there was a 3-year agreement being
developed to continue leasing the Riding Club to the current operator, with the possibility of
extending the lease 2 additional years. The Community Services Director recommended
inviting the new owners to a future Equestrian Committee so that they can learn the feelings
of the local equestrian community regarding their desire to re-zone the site.

PROPOSED TRAIL SAFETY PAMPHLET
The Community Services Director provided background to this agenda item noting that the
City had been considering the distribution of information on how to react to coyotes on the
trails and how to report trail vandalism, erosion issues, or other trail emergencies. He stated
that audience and PVPHA member, Sharon Yarber, had recently contacted him regarding the
dissemination of information to a growing number of new Peninsula residents who may not
know how to safely interact with equestrians on our local trails. The Community Services
Director also noted that the PVP Land Conservancy maintained several Peninsula trails and
had developed informational trail guides which could also be included in the proposed Trail
Safety Pamphlet.

MEMBER HARIK felt that the development of the Trail Safety Pamphlet was a good idea and
that it would may be wise to work with the School District and present the trail safety
information to school children.
EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
FEBRUARY 26, 2018  3
 Sharon Yarber, described several personal incidents that could have resulted in injuries to
horses, riders, and/or trail users. She felt it would be ideal to periodically promote the
information from the Trail Safety Pamphlet in the City’s Quarterly Newsletter, Peninsula
People magazine, on NextDoor, and by other methods.

The Community Services Director noted that he had discussed the possibility of developing a
2-sided, 3-fold, color pamphlet with other City staff if all the information would fit on it and
placing pamphlets in weather-proof, plastic distribution boxes with lids at key locations on the
City’s trails. He repeated his staff report recommendation that a Subcommittee be
established to assist in the development of the Trail Safety Pamphlet and no members
expressed interest in this project. It was therefore determined that City staff would work with
Sharon Yarber, other interested PVP Horsemens Association members, and PVP Land
Conservancy staff in developing a draft pamphlet for the Committee’s review at their next
meeting.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL SO ORDERED.

INCREASING ATTENDANCE AND PARTICIPATION  AT  CITY  CELEBRATION
EQUESTRIAN EVENTS AND ACTIVITIES
The Community Services Director briefly reviewed the staff report noting that tonight’s
discussion would be a continuation from the Equestrian Committee’s Special Meeting on
December 18, 2017. CHAIRMAN MITCHELL stated her belief that despite the suggestions
discussed thus far that the Ernie Howlett Park venue was too large and spread out to hold a
quality City Celebration event and that the needs of the Music Festival dominated the City’s
event. Several members concurred noting that most of the riders who participate in the Poker
Ride and equestrian events tend to come from the east side of the City. Therefore, it required
several truck and trailer trips to get the Junior Drill Team to Howlett Park and it was a long
ride on the City’s trails to and from the event for those who preferred to ride there. In addition,
Committee Members was felt that serving food from Food Trucks detracted from the former
barbecue food typically offered for sale at the City Celebration event. Thus, there was
agreement by Committee Members that the Empty Saddle Club was more conducive for
furtherance of the City’s equestrian heritage.

Discussion ensued regarding a proposed event timeline, food sales, activities, and equestrian
events that could occur at the Empty Saddle Club venue. The Community Services Director
reminded the Committee that during the last few years at the Empty Saddle Club that City
Celebration event attendance fell sharply after 3:00 or 4:00 p.m. He also noted that several
residents reported that Saturday mornings are very challenging for families who have their
children signed up for swim lessons, AYSO Soccer, karate classes, and other activities.
CHAIRMAN MITCHELL recommended starting the event at 11:00 a.m. and ending at 4:00
p.m. MEMBER PERSICHINA volunteered to coordinate the barbecue food offerings should
the Palos Verdes 4-H Club not be interested and to offer the popular Hay Rides around the
venue. MEMER SHINN noted that there were a limited number of corrals available should
Susie Lytal be asked to put together a Parade of Breeds event.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
FEBRUARY 26, 2018  4
 Audience member, Sean Martin suggested that in addition to the Poker Ride, a Junior Drill
Team demonstration, or other demonstrations, that a Battle for the Saddle event be offered as
culmination of several preliminary events offered throughout this year. Most Committee
Members felt that this event would draw a good number of local equestrian spectators to
attend the City Celebration.

In regards to potentially moving the event back to the Empty Saddle Club, the Community
Services Director noted that this Club held several annual Fall events, including a Cowboy
Days event and a Cowboy Poetry event. In addition, the September 15, 2018 event date was
very firm, as any other Saturday in September would have conflicts with home college football
games, the Portuguese Bend National Horse Show, and/or conflicts with Jewish holiday
periods. If the Committee voted to make a recommendation to move the City Celebration
event back to the Empty Saddle Club, he agreed to immediately contact President, Greg
Keenan, as to its availability on this date.

MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER HARIK

  TO RECOMMEND THAT THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MAKE A
  RECOMMENDATION TO CITY COUNCIL TO MOVE THE 2018 CITY CELEBRATION
  EVENT BACK TO THE EMPTY SADDLE CLUB VENUE, IF AVAILABLE ON
  SEPTEMBER 15, 2018.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL SO ORDERED.

EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG
HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL RECEIVED AND FILED THE REPORT.

COMMITTEE MEMBER REPORTS
A.  ADOPT-A-TRAIL REPORTS
  MEMBER SHINN thanked City staff for recently grooming many of the City’s trails.
  Audience Member, Nancy Wildman suggested that Doggie Bag dispensers be installed
  at key sites on the City’s trails to reduce the amount of dog droppings on the trails.
B.  ANNUAL LICENSED HORSE TRAINERS MEETING – FEBRUARY 26, 2018
  MEMBER SHINN reported that the meeting went well, noting there was concern
  expressed about the lack of riders attending the recreational riding only periods on
  weekends and holidays at Chandler Park horse arena. It was agreed that this rule and
  whether horses could be turned out in this arena would be discussed at the March 26,
  2018 Equestrian Committee meeting. Other Trainer suggestions included adding more
  jump poles and rakes to the Howlett Park arenas, installing a manual sprinkler control
  on Dapplegray Park’s junior dressage arena, having City Code Enforcement staff
  contact the residents at #4 Goldring Place to keep their dogs from scaring horse riders
  on the trail next to their rear fence, and to notify the First Baptist Church on Moccasin
  Lane that their rear fence is falling onto the bridle trail.
EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
FEBRUARY 26, 2018  5
 FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS
A.  PV PENINSULA WATER RELIABILITY PROJECT UPDATE – Monthly

B.  DRAFT MAYOR’S BREAKFAST RIDE FLYER – March 26, 2018

C.  DRAFT TRAIL SAFETY PAMPHLET – March 26, 2018

D.  REVIEW OF CHANDLER PARK ARENA RULES – March 26, 2018

E.  INCREASING THE NUMBER OF JUMP POLES AND RAKES AT THE HOWLETT
  PARK ARENAS – March 26, 2018

ADJOURNMENT
MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER SILVANO

  TO ADJOURN THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN MITCHELL ADJOURNED THE MEETING.

The meeting adjourned at 8:20 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,

Andy Clark
Community Services Director
